clauses.reason: lead: Lead: prescribes, under sec. 301 of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the regulations governing the payment of basic allowances for subsistence to members of the uniformed services. Ends with the whole order: express revocation by EO 11157 sec. 502(a), effective on signing 1964-06-22. The clause has no own-term end, sunset or termination wording of its own that falls before this end.

clauses.reason: sec1: Sec. 1: enlisted members subsisted in kind in a mess, whose duties take them from station for one or more meals, are entitled for each such meal to one-third of the daily basic allowance (as issued; changed by EO 10605 in 1955). Ends with the whole order: express revocation by EO 11157 sec. 502(a), effective on signing 1964-06-22. The clause has no own-term end, sunset or termination wording of its own that falls before this end. Partial change before the end: EO 10605 (1955-04-22) rewrote this section, attached as a later event; it did not end the clause.

later_events.mechanism: amendment of sec. 1: EO 10605 amends sec. 1 to read that enlisted members subsisted in kind but absent from station for a meal are entitled for each meal to 'a pro-rated share' (replacing 'one-third') of the daily basic allowance for subsistence, and authorizes the Secretaries of Defense, the Treasury and Commerce to fix the amount of the share, uniform for all services; it states no effective date, so effective on signing, April 22, 1955 (20 FR 2747). It changes the clause and does not end it; EO 10605 was itself revoked by EO 11157 sec. 502(e) on the same day as EO 10119.

clauses.mechanism: own-term sunset in sec. 4 ('Provided, that all such regulations and determinations shall cease to be effective on May 1, 1950') read with sec. 5 (secs. 1-3 become effective on May 1, 1950): the transitional adoption of the existing subsistence-allowance regulations and determinations, effective immediately on signing (1950-03-27), lapses on 1950-05-01, the day the order's own regulations (secs. 1-3) take over
clauses.reason: Sec. 4: adopts and prescribes, so far as applicable and appropriate, the existing Executive-order and departmental regulations on subsistence allowances under the Pay Readjustment Act of 1942 as regulations authorized by sec. 301 of the Career Compensation Act, and says all of them cease to be effective on May 1, 1950. The stated date is a fixed own-term sunset (not a report deadline or a condition), and no held text extends it, so this clause first ends on 1950-05-01, long before the revocation. EO 11157 sec. 502(a) later revoked the whole order (1964-06-22); recorded as a later event.

clauses.reason: sec5: Sec. 5: sec. 4 effective immediately and secs. 1-3 effective May 1, 1950. A timing clause; once May 1, 1950 passed it was spent, but a spent clause stays part of the order until the order is revoked. Ends with the whole order: express revocation by EO 11157 sec. 502(a), effective on signing 1964-06-22. The clause has no own-term end, sunset or termination wording of its own that falls before this end.

savings.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_11157 (EO 11157, 29 FR 7973-7980, read once in full): sec. 502 revokes EO 10119 (a) and its amendment EO 10605 (e) with no savings, pending-matter or exception clause and no effective-date wording; Part III (secs. 301-303) re-prescribes the subsistence-allowance rules of EO 10119 as amended under 37 U.S.C. 402 (pro-rated meal share, supplemental regulations by the Secretaries, the same five definitions), and secs. 302 and 407 grant fresh authority to issue supplementary regulations. Own-residual check, reading EO 10119 in full (secs. 1-5): it created no fund, office or right (the allowances rest on sec. 301 of the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and its successor in 37 U.S.C. 402), but its secs. 1-3 are the source of the regulations that sec. 302 of EO 11157 carries forward, and sec. 2 supplemental regulations issued by the Secretaries under it were not revoked by their terms. S0 prefill (none_after_bounded_search) OVERRULED to transferred_or_accrued: the revoked order's content and delegation were transferred to the successor order (Part III) and allowances already earned under it accrued under the statute. Bounded search: EO 10119, EO 10605 and EO 11157 in full; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 10119 named only in EO 10605 and EO 11157).

research_rationale: EO 10119 (signed 1950-03-27, 15 FR 1767), read in full from the held FR text, prescribes regulations for basic allowances for subsistence to members of the uniformed services (secs. 1-3), adopts the existing regulations in a transitional section (sec. 4, which sets May 1, 1950 as the day all such regulations cease to be effective) and sets effective dates (sec. 5: sec. 4 immediately, secs. 1-3 on May 1, 1950). The machine own-term leads are a sunset_date (sec. 4, 1950-05-01) and conditions (the Secretaries' supplemental regulations); only the sec. 4 date is a stated end, and it ends only sec. 4. EO 11157 (read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_11157.json) sec. 502(a) revokes the order, effective on signing 1964-06-22. EO 10605 (20 FR 2747, held FR text, read in full) amended sec. 1 on 1955-04-22 and is attached as a later event on the sec. 1 clause; it was revoked with the order by EO 11157 sec. 502(e). The dossier's record ACT:EO:10119>EO:10605 quotes an American Presidency Project transcription, so the amendment is attached by the id of the held official FR text, ACTOR_TEXT:EO:10605, instead; the dossier lists no missing provision. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 10119 named only in EO 10605 and EO 11157 (other hits are page numbers and neighbouring documents). Inventory correction: the dossier's seven clauses mis-segment the order (sec. 1 and 2 merged, sec. 3(c) spanning two pages of furniture, secs. 4 and 5 folded into one clause) and include a spurious 'sec1-b-dup2' that is a Commodity Credit Corporation rule printed on the same page; inventory_overrides replace them with twelve clauses (lead, secs. 1, 2, 3 lead, 3(a)-(e) with 3(c) in two fragments, 4 and 5). Savings: the S0 prefill is overruled, see savings_residuals.
